title: per-block FP8 MMQ prefill kernel — the arm meant to be BOTH exact and fast
question: cuBLASLt refuses block-scaled FP8 on sm_120 (per-tensor SCALAR only). ARM A folds the block-128 grid to one per-tensor scale: +18.4% pp512 but the greedy stream diverges at pos 20 — not shippable. ARM B' dequants on-device to Q8_0: bit-exact but rides the Q8_0 MMQ, i.e. the floor. This lane built P1 option (b): our OWN MMQ tile consuming the checkpoint's e4m3 bytes and its per-[128x128] f32 scale grid directly.
verdict: EXACTNESS: DELIVERED. PERFORMANCE: NEGATIVE — the kernel does not beat the Q8_0 MMQ floor it was written to replace, at any 27B projection shape, at m=512 or m=6257, at any token tile in the sweep. The arm is exact and it is not fast, so it does not clear its own reason for existing. Kept behind MEMRA_FP8_MMQ=1, default OFF.

section: 1. KERNEL-CHECK (the mandatory gate — bit-identity vs a host reference of the SAME arithmetic)

arms.EXACT: integer e4m3 codes, power-of-two block scales, activation amax pinned to exactly 448 so the activation quantizer is exact too. Gated at ulp_mismatch == 0 AND nan == 0 — bit-identity, not a tolerance.
arms.RAND: general random operands, gated at rms_rel < 1e-5 (the GEMM-standard error metric: max_abs / rms(want))

shapes: 9, including the ragged cases the block grid makes non-trivial: out_f not a multiple of 128 (128x200, 384x320), in_f with a k tail (144x128, 272x136), the real 5120x1536, and m=1
result: ALL GREEN. Every EXACT row 0/N bit mismatches and 0 NaN; every RAND row rms_rel <= 1.24e-6. Re-run on this session's HEAD after the counter edits — still ALL GREEN. Also ALL GREEN at every swept tile size (X=32/64/128/256), so the tile geometry does not touch exactness.

section: 2. MODEL-LEVEL EXACTNESS (which bar branch applied, and why)
bar: the task set two branches: (a) if the MMQ greedy stream is BIT-IDENTICAL to the ARM B'/floor stream, report stream identity; (b) if the streams differ, the verdict needs the kernel-check bit-identity above (mandatory) PLUS the honest note that per-block-FP8 arithmetic is not Q8_0-requant arithmetic, with a 6-draw sampled loop and a quality sanity instead of stream identity.
branch_applied: (b). The streams differ, and they differ for the reason branch (b) anticipates: this kernel accumulates per-block FP8 products in f32, while the floor re-quantizes the same weights to Q8_0 and accumulates int8 in s32. Different arithmetic path, not a bug — and the negative control proves the instrument can see a real bug when there is one.
coverage: FULL, measured: 1568 of 1576 prefill-GEMM hook entries dispatched through the kernel on the 1.7B block-128 checkpoint = 99.5% (the 8 refusals are the tied-embedding lm_head, which has no F8 source tensor). Floor control on the same binary: identical 1576 entries, all refused at the env gate, zero dispatches, different stream digest — so the digest difference is the kernel, not run-to-run noise. Receipt: coverage-ledger-1p7b.log.

A VRAM-ceiling fact about the duplicating stash at long context, not a kernel bug: pp512 at the same budget ran 5/5 clean.

Zero bad_shape, zero bad_scale, zero NaN refusals: no precondition of the kernel rejects a single 27B projection. Matches the independent byte prediction (~355 MiB e4m3/layer, BUDGET=3072 => a prefix of ~8.6 of 64 layers).
27b_verify_path: 0 dispatches AND 0 hook ENTRIES. decode_step_t emits each layer's mixer input directly as q8_1 and drops the f32 h, so matmul_pre's x_raw_ok guard turns off every raw-f32 prefill arm there. Consequence worth recording loudly: MEMRA_PREFILL_LOGITS (added in this lane) dumps THAT vector, so both arms compute it on the FLOOR and its 0.000e0 is NOT an exactness result. A false-positive 'bit-identical' was caught this way and is documented rather than buried.

The MMQ arm needs the duplicating stash. So the 27B mmq-vs-arma pp comparison is coverage-asymmetric BY CONSTRUCTION, which is exactly why the GEMM-only bench exists.

section: 5. MECHANISM — why the kernel is exact and still slow
finding: both arms land at 105-127 TFLOP against the 381-TF class the .kind::f8f6f4 MMA can reach, so NEITHER arm is MMA-bound. The whole premise of this kernel — e4m3 x e4m3 native MMA, weight tile is a pure byte copy, zero decode — buys an advantage on an axis that is not the bottleneck. Nor is there a bandwidth win to collect: e4m3 moves 1.0 B/weight vs Q8_0's 34/32 = 1.0625, a 6% read edge. What differs is per-tile work: the Q8_0 tile accumulates int8 products in s32 with ONE f32 fold at the very end, while this tile carries an f32 accumulator and folds (s_blk * dB) per k-block. The scale-row hoist already reduced the scale fetch to two scalar loads per 256-k iteration, so what remains is the f32 accumulate/fold itself — structural to per-block FP8 as formulated here, not a tuning miss. The tile sweep independently confirms it: no geometry reaches the floor.

one_paragraph: Stop trying to win inside a k-blocked f32 accumulator and attack the two facts the profile actually shows: nobody is MMA-bound, and the floor wins because it defers ALL scaling to one epilogue fold. A v2 should make per-block FP8 look like that — keep the weight bytes verbatim (the exactness win is real and cheap: the tile loader is a pure int4 copy), but restructure so the 128-wide scale block is the OUTER k loop and the inner 128-k run accumulates in a single unscaled tensor-core accumulator, folding s_blk once per block into a separate f32 running sum. That is arithmetically the same per-block product this kernel already proves exact, with one fold per 128 k instead of per 256-k iteration of mixed f32 work, and it makes the inner loop structurally identical to the floor's (which is the thing that measured faster). Since the ceiling is not the MMA, the second half of the win has to come from occupancy and overlap, not a bigger tile: at 105-127 TFLOP with 1 CTA/SM on a 61 KB smem tile the kernel is latency-exposed, so the same treatment the w4a8 lane got — halve the row tile and the warp count together (MMQ_Y and nwarps move as a pair, which does not duplicate weight reads) to buy 2 CTA/SM, and cp.async double-buffer the weight tile against the MMA — is where the remaining 20% and then ARM A's 18% live. If that lands, per-block exactness beats ARM A's lossy fold on both axes; if a rebuilt inner loop still cannot reach the floor, the honest conclusion is that per-block FP8 has no prefill advantage on sm_120 and the exact path should stay ARM B' (device dequant to Q8_0), whose only cost is a one-time load-time pass.

shippable: the kernel is correct and gated OFF (MEMRA_FP8_MMQ=1 opt-in). No default flips. No board-moving numbers, so no perf-board regeneration is owed. Per the flags doctrine a concluded-negative arm should have its flag and dispatch arm killed — the JSONL row is the record — but this arm is the only exact per-block-FP8 consumer in the tree and the v2 above rebuilds its inner loop, so it is left in place as the seam that work starts from rather than deleted and rewritten. That is an owner call to confirm, not a decision this lane takes.
